collection_summary: This instance is a curator-bounded ground truth listing 16 major architectural styles commonly covered in survey-canon textbook treatments of the history of architecture, with global coverage including 4 non-Western styles (Mesoamerican, Japanese, Moorish, Mughal) per audit-recommended civilizational balance. For each style the staged row records a curator-selected single landmark building (most-iconic example per textbook convention), the modern-day country of the landmark's site location, and the year of completion per the per-building Wikipedia article's infobox or documented exception. The 16-row universe is honestly characterized as candidate_rebuild rather than source-defined — no single Wikipedia master article maps 'architectural style → single landmark building'; the universe is curator-bounded survey-canon coverage. The schema is designed for qualitative benchmark evaluation: Architectural Style is the PK lookup target; Landmark Building is text exact-match (single canonical title per style); Modern-day Country is text exact-match from an 11-distinct-value vocabulary; Year of Completion is integer exact-match.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (History_of_architecture): universe-context (provides the period-by-style textbook narrative spanning ancient through 20th-century architectural traditions; supplies the survey-canon framing rationale for the 16-row slate).
- source_urls[1] (List_of_architectural_styles): style-candidate master (sectioned article listing architectural styles by period and region; includes dedicated sections for non-Western styles — Mesoamerican, East Asian, Islamic, Mughal — that ground the 4 non-Western universe additions).
- source_urls[2-17] (16 per-style articles): canonical Style name + Landmark Building example grounding. Each style's Wikipedia article provides (a) the canonical style PK label matching the article title, and (b) listed examples of canonical buildings from which the staged Landmark Building is curator-selected per the Landmark Rule documented in normalization_decisions.
- source_urls[18-33] (16 per-building articles): Modern-day Country + Year of Completion grounding. Each building's Wikipedia article provides the country of site location and the completion year via infobox Completed/Built fields OR article-body completion statements, with documented range/approximation conventions per the Year Rule. The Year Rule's infobox-priority clause applies where the infobox has a literal 'Completed' field; for buildings whose infobox uses non-'Completed' fields (e.g., 'Founded' / 'Consecrated') or whose completion year appears in the article body rather than the infobox (e.g., Speyer Cathedral 1106 from body 'Speyer II was completed in 1106'; Casa Batlló 1906 from body 'completed in 1906'; Villa Savoye 1931 from lead 'built between 1928 and 1931'), the staged year is supported by the body or non-infobox infobox-field per the Year Rule's body-supported allowance.

Multi-source Tier B instance (source_count = 34 = 2 master + 16 per-style + 16 per-building). The 34-URL plan over the 18-URL alternative (2 master + 16 per-style only) was selected because Modern-day Country and Year of Completion are answer-key cells grounded by per-building articles — the per-building articles should be explicitly in source_urls rather than consulted-but-not-cited per audit recommendation. Cell-level audit can spot-check Style PK against per-style article titles; Landmark Building against per-style article example lists; Modern-day Country and Year of Completion against per-building article infoboxes.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass (after TWO rounds of pre-staging audit design review — see post-staging cycle-0 notes below). Universe (16 textbook-canon architectural styles with global coverage) is honestly characterized as curator-bounded candidate_rebuild; per-row attribute cells are verbatim/lightly-normalized from per-style + per-building Wikipedia articles. Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical iconic landmarks; mid-difficulty cells include textbook-canonical extensions; harder calibration cells include the non-Western and approximate-year rows. Row count (16) clears the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected after picker recommendation for 'saturate qualitative to 5/5' option; TWO rounds of pre-staging audit design review (Round 1: 5 design issues; Round 2: 3 additional fixes after Round 1 revisions) resolved 8 design-level issues before any files were written.
- Category: qualitative (gap 1 before this staging — `qualitative` at 4 of 5 with major_music_genres_landmark_albums, major_western_philosophers_primary_works, us_states_warm_year_round_climate, major_religious_traditions_foundational_texts; this instance SATURATES qualitative at 5/5 — SEVENTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5, factual_lookup 6/5 over-target, top_k 6/5 over-target).
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, multi-source; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 34 (2 master + 16 per-style + 16 per-building per audit recommendation).
- Expected shape: 16 rows × 4 columns; PK = Architectural Style.
- Domain: Culture/Architecture — NEW Architecture subdomain extending the Culture family from 9 to 10 instances.
- Entity class: abstract-categories/architectural-styles — NEW fine-class extending the abstract-categories bucket from 3 fine-classes (music-genres, religions, languages) to 4. Subject-wins pattern (PK = abstract-category subject; answer = landmark example).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) curator-bounded universe — the 16-row survey-canon slate is principled but judgment-based; honestly signaled via claim_type = candidate_rebuild. (b) Landmark Building cell is curator-selected from per-style article examples per the explicit Landmark Rule documented in normalization_decisions. (c) Year of Completion uses the per-building infobox 'Completed'/'Built' field OR article-body completion statement per the Year Rule, with explicit documented exceptions for 5 buildings (Great Pyramid c. 2600 BC, Pyramid of the Sun c. 200 AD, Versailles 1715 largely-completed, Alhambra 1391 Nasrid-palace apogee, Hōryū-ji 607 infobox-completion despite the current complex's 711 reconstruction). (d) Modern-day Country uses modern-day sovereign-country names not civilization-of-origin per the Country Rule (Hagia Sophia = Turkey, Pantheon = Italy, Great Pyramid = Egypt). (e) Style PK labels match Wikipedia article canonical titles (with 'architecture' suffix for most: Ancient Egyptian architecture, Gothic architecture, etc.; without suffix for Art Nouveau / Art Deco which are canonical without the suffix). (f) Western-tradition weight: 12 of 16 rows are Western/Euro-Mediterranean styles vs 4 non-Western — the 16-row variant was selected over a 12-row Western-only variant per audit Round 1 recommendation to expand for global coverage.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets architectural styles, buildings, or qualitative engineered-physical-aesthetic instances.

Why 16-row global universe rather than alternatives: TWO rounds of pre-staging audit design review evaluated 3 universe options. Option A (12-row Western/Euro-Mediterranean only) was rejected per Round 1 audit feedback because the cited Wikipedia 'List of architectural styles' explicitly covers Islamic, South Asian, East Asian, Pre-Columbian, and African styles — a 12-row Western-only slate would look under-bounded relative to the source. Option B (16-row global, the chosen design) adds 4 non-Western styles (Mesoamerican, Japanese, Moorish, Mughal) for civilizational balance per audit-recommended path. Option C (15-row with Western-narrowed title) was rejected as less benchmark-rich than Option B.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: qualitative pairs reasonably with operation_type=projection per references/artifact-contract.md. The 3-attribute SELECT per row (Landmark Building + Modern-day Country + Year of Completion) over the curator-bounded entity universe is the canonical qualitative-projection primitive (matching the 4-col SELECT pattern of music_genres_landmark_albums and religious_traditions_foundational_texts).

Domain selection: Culture/Architecture — NEW Architecture subdomain. Culture is already a large family (9 instances). Architecture is a NEW subdomain that complements the existing aesthetic-subdomains (Film, Music, Literature, Visual Arts, Philosophy). The Culture/Architecture combination is appropriate for engineered-physical-aesthetic instances.

Entity class selection: abstract-categories/architectural-styles — NEW fine-class within abstract-categories bucket. The bucket has 3 existing fine-classes (music-genres, religions, languages); this instance brings it to 4 fine-classes. NEW fine-class scores strong on the Entity-class novelty axis. Per the entity-class policy, this uses the subject-wins exception: PK = Architectural Style (abstract-category subject), answer entity = Landmark Building (engineered-structures, would also be a valid classification but subject-wins applies for closed-vocab style subjects).

Claim type: candidate_rebuild — confirmed by audit Round 2 as appropriate. No clean source-defined master maps 'major architectural style → single landmark building'. List of architectural styles is useful as a candidate source but is broad, sectioned, and marked as needing rewrite, so it cannot be treated as a closed authoritative universe. claim_type matches the precedent set by major_western_philosophers_primary_works, major_religious_traditions_foundational_texts, and major_music_genres_landmark_albums.

Pre-staging audit review history:

ROUND 1 (2026-05-15): audit agent identified 5 design-level issues with the initial 12-row Western-only proposal. (a) Universe scope overclaim: 'major architectural styles' was too strong for a 12-row Western-only slate omitting non-Western traditions per the cited Wikipedia source's sectioned non-Western coverage. (b) Year column not source-stable: Great Pyramid -2560 didn't match article's 'c. 2600 BC'; Versailles 1682 was court-history not completion date per article. (c) Source plan missing per-style sources: per-building articles alone don't consistently ground 'this is the single most-iconic example of the style'. (d) Country column should be renamed 'Modern-day Country' for unambiguous semantics. (e) claim_type=candidate_rebuild confirmed appropriate.

ROUND 2 (2026-05-15): audit agent verified Round 1 fixes applied (universe expanded to 16 rows with 4 non-Western additions; Country renamed; Versailles 1715; Great Pyramid -2600; 34-URL source plan with per-style articles; 4 normalization rules written into normalization_decisions). Round 2 surfaced 3 additional pre-staging fixes: (f) Canonicalize Style PKs to match Wikipedia article titles ('Ancient Egyptian architecture' not 'Ancient Egyptian'; 'Japanese architecture' not 'East Asian'; 'Moorish architecture' not 'Islamic'; etc.). (g) Hōryū-ji year semantics: infobox 'Completed 607' vs article body's '711 reconstruction of the current complex' — use 607 per infobox rule. (h) Alhambra year 1370 not source-stable: article says construction began 1238 and Palace of the Lions built during Muhammad V's second reign 1362-1391 — use 1391 per 'latest year in range' rule under the Year Rule's range clause, documented as keyed to Palace of the Lions / Nasrid-palace apogee. All 3 Round 2 fixes applied in cycle-0 staging.

Post-audit (2026-05-15, cycle 1): cycle-1 audit verdict 'Ready' — 0 BLOCKING, 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The data-level checks all passed: 16 rows × 4 cols, PK unique, schema/source_count consistent, source-grounding spot-checks passed for all 16 Landmark Building / Modern-day Country / Year of Completion cells per per-style article + per-building article references. The single hygiene finding was prose-only Year-source narrative drift: (a) source_coverage_notes overstated 'infobox Completed year' grounding when 3 rows (Speyer Cathedral 1106, Casa Batlló 1906, Villa Savoye 1931) are actually grounded by article-body completion statements rather than a literal infobox 'Completed' field; (b) normalization_decisions Year-normalization paragraph had an inconsistent 11/12 count split (said 'Direct-from-infobox cells (11 rows)' but parenthetical listed 12 rows; said 'Documented-exception cells (5 rows)' but listed only 4). Post-audit (2026-05-15, cycle 2): cycle-2 verification audit verdict 'Ready with residual hygiene' — 0 BLOCKING, 1 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The cycle-1 Year-source prose fixes were confirmed clean except for a count-arithmetic error in the cycle-1 normalization_decisions Year-normalization paragraph: the '6 rows' enumeration actually covered 8 rows (bullets a-e were 5 individual rows + bullet (f) covered 3 individual buildings Speyer/Casa Batlló/Villa Savoye); the 'remaining 9' direct-infobox claim listed only 8 rows plus a parenthetical double-count of Hōryū-ji. Post-audit (2026-05-15, cycle 3): cycle-3 verification audit verdict 'Ready+Clean' — 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. The cycle-2 Year-normalization 3-way split (4 + 3 + 9 = 16) confirmed clean: every landmark appears exactly once in exactly one bucket; Hōryū-ji listed only in the direct-infobox bucket with reconstructed-complex caveat inline (no double-count). Data state confirmed: 16 rows, schema unchanged, unique Architectural Style PK, alphabetical sort intact, Modern-day Country distribution intact (France 3 / Italy 2 / Germany 2 / Spain 2 / 7 singletons), Year range -2600 to 1931, source_count = 34. Instance marked accept-ready as of 2026-05-15. Total cycle count: 4 (cycle-0 staging + cycles 1-3 audit/repair, all 0 BLOCKING). The instance SATURATES `qualitative` at 5/5 — **SEVENTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR** after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5, factual_lookup 6/5 over-target, top_k 6/5 over-target. normalization_decisions:
Universe definition: the staged universe is the 16 architectural styles commonly covered in survey-canon textbook treatments of the history of architecture, with global coverage including 4 non-Western styles (Mesoamerican architecture, Japanese architecture, Moorish architecture, Mughal architecture) for civilizational balance over a 12-row Western-only alternative. The universe boundary is curator-bounded survey-canon coverage rather than source-defined ranking — no single Wikipedia master article maps 'architectural style → single landmark building'. The 16 staged styles: Ancient Egyptian architecture, Ancient Greek architecture, Ancient Roman architecture, Art Deco, Art Nouveau, Baroque architecture, Byzantine architecture, Gothic architecture, Japanese architecture, Mesoamerican architecture, Modern architecture, Moorish architecture, Mughal architecture, Neoclassical architecture, Renaissance architecture, Romanesque architecture.

4 EXPLICIT NORMALIZATION RULES (per audit Round 1 recommendation, applied in cycle-0):

(1) UNIVERSE RULE: 'Selected survey-canon architectural styles spanning ancient through 20th-century traditions, with global coverage including 4 non-Western styles per the audit-recommended expansion path. The 16-row slate is curator-bounded textbook-canon coverage rather than source-defined ranking.'

(2) LANDMARK RULE: 'Landmark Building is curator-selected from the per-style Wikipedia article's listed examples / textbook convention, NOT source-defined ranking. Selection precedence: (a) the building most commonly cited in textbook surveys of the style, (b) for ties, the earliest-completed canonical example, (c) for ties between secular and religious examples, the one with broader international name-recognition.'

(3) YEAR RULE: 'Use the per-building Wikipedia article's completion year as supported by (a) the infobox Completed/Built field when present, OR (b) the article body or lead's completion statement when the infobox uses a non-Completed field (Founded/Consecrated/etc.) or when the infobox lacks a Completed field entirely. If only a range exists, use the latest year of the canonical-style completion. If only an approximate (c./circa) year exists, encode the approximate year and document. For destroyed/reconstructed landmarks, use the infobox-Completed-field value per default (NOT the reconstruction year unless infobox specifies otherwise).'

(4) COUNTRY RULE: 'Modern-day sovereign country of site location, NOT civilization-of-origin (Hagia Sophia = Turkey, not Byzantine; Pantheon = Italy, not Roman Empire; Great Pyramid = Egypt; Brandenburg Gate = Germany, not Prussia).'

Architectural Style normalization: each row's Architectural Style PK is taken from the corresponding Wikipedia per-style article's canonical title. 14 of 16 PKs use the 'X architecture' pattern (Ancient Egyptian architecture, Ancient Greek architecture, Ancient Roman architecture, Byzantine architecture, Romanesque architecture, Gothic architecture, Renaissance architecture, Baroque architecture, Neoclassical architecture, Modern architecture, Mesoamerican architecture, Japanese architecture, Moorish architecture, Mughal architecture); 2 PKs use the bare style name without the 'architecture' suffix per the Wikipedia article's canonical title (Art Nouveau, Art Deco). The 'East Asian' label is staged as 'Japanese architecture' per audit Round 2 — Hōryū-ji is specifically Japanese rather than broader East Asian. The 'Islamic' label is staged as 'Moorish architecture' per audit Round 2 — Alhambra is specifically Moorish (Iberian Islamic) rather than broader pan-Islamic.

Landmark Building normalization: each row's Landmark Building is taken from the per-building Wikipedia article's canonical title. The cell preserves source's compound naming ('Pantheon, Rome' with comma-disambiguation; 'Hōryū-ji' with diacritic). Per-row landmark-selection rationale (per Landmark Rule):

  - Ancient Egyptian architecture → Great Pyramid of Giza: most-iconic Egyptian pyramid; sole surviving Wonder of the Ancient World; canonical Egyptian-architecture example.
  - Ancient Greek architecture → Parthenon: most-iconic Greek temple; canonical Doric-order Pentelic-marble example.
  - Ancient Roman architecture → Pantheon, Rome: best-preserved Roman monument; canonical Roman-dome example.
  - Mesoamerican architecture → Pyramid of the Sun: largest pre-Columbian structure in Mesoamerica; canonical Teotihuacan example.
  - Byzantine architecture → Hagia Sophia: most-iconic Byzantine basilica; canonical pendentive-supported-dome example.
  - Japanese architecture → Hōryū-ji: oldest extant wooden building in the world (reconstructed c. 711); canonical Asuka-period Japanese Buddhist architecture example.
  - Romanesque architecture → Speyer Cathedral: largest Romanesque cathedral; canonical German Romanesque example with Salian-imperial significance.
  - Gothic architecture → Notre-Dame de Paris: most-LLM-iconic Gothic cathedral; canonical Early Gothic example with rose-window-and-flying-buttress vocabulary.
  - Moorish architecture → Alhambra: most-iconic Moorish palace complex; canonical Nasrid-dynasty example combining geometric tilework, muqarnas, and water-garden architecture.
  - Renaissance architecture → Florence Cathedral: earliest completed Renaissance icon (1436 Brunelleschi dome); canonical example of Renaissance dome engineering succeeding Roman antecedents.
  - Mughal architecture → Taj Mahal: most-iconic Mughal mausoleum; canonical Mughal-architecture example combining Persian, Islamic, and Indian traditions.
  - Baroque architecture → Palace of Versailles: most-iconic Baroque palace; canonical secular-Baroque grand-ensemble example.
  - Neoclassical architecture → Brandenburg Gate: most-iconic Neoclassical city gate; canonical Doric-order Greek-revival monument.
  - Art Nouveau → Casa Batlló: most-iconic Catalan Modernisme/Art-Nouveau facade; canonical Gaudí example.
  - Art Deco → Chrysler Building: most-iconic Art Deco skyscraper; canonical streamlined-vertical-ornament example.
  - Modern architecture → Villa Savoye: most-iconic International Style residence; canonical Le-Corbusier-Five-Points-of-Architecture example.

Modern-day Country normalization: each row's Modern-day Country is the modern-day sovereign country of site location per the Country Rule. Country distribution (11 distinct): France 3 (Notre-Dame de Paris, Palace of Versailles, Villa Savoye), Italy 2 (Pantheon Rome, Florence Cathedral), Germany 2 (Speyer Cathedral, Brandenburg Gate), Spain 2 (Alhambra, Casa Batlló), Egypt 1 (Great Pyramid), Greece 1 (Parthenon), United States 1 (Chrysler Building), Turkey 1 (Hagia Sophia), Japan 1 (Hōryū-ji), Mexico 1 (Pyramid of the Sun), India 1 (Taj Mahal).

Year of Completion normalization: each row's Year of Completion is an integer year per the Year Rule. The 16 rows split 3 ways per Year-rule provenance. Rows requiring special interpretation under the Year Rule's circa-year and range-clause (4 rows): (a) Great Pyramid of Giza -2600 (c. 2600 BC per article's standard chronology — circa-year clause); (b) Pyramid of the Sun 200 (c. 200 AD per article's Founded date — circa-year clause); (c) Palace of Versailles 1715 (largely-completed-by-Louis-XIV's-death per article's primary completion-period statement — range-clause exception, latest year of canonical-style completion); (d) Alhambra 1391 (Palace of the Lions / Nasrid-palace apogee under Muhammad V's second reign 1362-1391 — range-clause, latest year of canonical-Moorish-style completion). Rows supported by article-body completion statements rather than literal infobox 'Completed' fields per the Year Rule's body-supported allowance (3 rows): Speyer Cathedral 1106 (body: 'Speyer II was completed in 1106'); Casa Batlló 1906 (body: 'completed in 1906'); Villa Savoye 1931 (lead: 'built between 1928 and 1931'). Rows with direct infobox-Completed support per the Year Rule's infobox-priority default (9 rows): Parthenon -432, Pantheon Rome 126, Hagia Sophia 537, Hōryū-ji 607 (infobox 'Completed 607' per default; the original burned 670 and the current complex was probably completed around 711, but the staged year follows the infobox-priority default — Year Rule's reconstructed-complex exception clause is documented but NOT invoked for this row), Notre-Dame 1345, Florence Cathedral 1436, Taj Mahal 1653, Brandenburg Gate 1791, Chrysler Building 1930. Total: 4 + 3 + 9 = 16 rows.

Sort order: CSV is sorted alphabetically by Architectural Style PK ascending (benchmark default for qualitative single-PK lookup tables). Sort produces Ancient Egyptian architecture / Ancient Greek architecture / Ancient Roman architecture / Art Deco / Art Nouveau / Baroque architecture / Byzantine architecture / Gothic architecture / Japanese architecture / Mesoamerican architecture / Modern architecture / Moorish architecture / Mughal architecture / Neoclassical architecture / Renaissance architecture / Romanesque architecture.
open_questions: 1. Whether the universe should expand beyond 16 rows to include additional textbook-canon styles (e.g., Brutalism, Postmodern, Beaux-Arts, Victorian / Gothic Revival, International Style separately from Modern). Current 16-row staging mirrors the 16-row religious_traditions precedent. 2. Whether the Hōryū-ji year should be 607 (current staging, per infobox 'Completed') or 711 (current complex completion after the 670 fire). Current staging uses 607 per Year Rule's infobox-priority default; a reconstructed-complex exception clause is documented but not invoked for this row. 3. Whether the Alhambra year should be 1391 (current staging, Palace of the Lions apogee) or 1238 (construction-began year per article's earliest date) or another year keyed to a different Alhambra phase. 4. Whether the Pyramid of the Sun year should be 200 (current staging, per Founded date) or a range like 100-250 AD reflecting the broader construction-period uncertainty. 5. Whether the 'Architectural Style' PK should use the 'X architecture' suffix uniformly (would push Art Nouveau → 'Art Nouveau architecture' and Art Deco → 'Art Deco architecture' to match the other 14 rows; current staging follows Wikipedia article titles which leave these 2 without the suffix). 6. Whether the Renaissance row's Landmark Building should be Florence Cathedral (current staging, earliest-completed Renaissance icon 1436) or St. Peter's Basilica (universally-iconic but Renaissance-to-Baroque transitional). 7. Whether the Baroque row's Landmark Building should be Palace of Versailles (current staging, secular Baroque palace) or a religious Baroque example like Karlskirche (Vienna, cleaner infobox year 1737) or St. Peter's Basilica (Bernini elements). 8. Whether the universe should include both a Western-style row and a non-Western-style row for the same chronological period (e.g., Gothic 1345 + Mughal 1653 + Mesoamerican 200 spread Western and non-Western temporally rather than period-paired). Current staging is style-per-row without period-pairing.
